title: Duplicate embeddings generated when re-ingesting the same repository
body: `_check_skip()` in `ingestion/pipeline.py` passes the string `"IngestedSource"` to `db_session.query()` instead of the model class from `core/models/ingested_source.py`. The query fails, a broad `except Exception` catches it, and the source isn't skipped. It's chunked and embedded again.

title: Add support for ingesting a portfolio website URL
body: Allow users to submit a URL to their personal portfolio site. The pipeline should fetch the page content, extract relevant text (bio, project descriptions), and include it in the vector store alongside GitHub and resume data.

title: Add a content hash to detect unchanged documents and skip re-embedding
body: When a user re-submits the same README without changes, the pipeline should detect that the content hash hasn't changed and skip the embedding step, reducing unnecessary API calls.

title: Add support for parsing GitHub Actions workflow files to detect CI/CD skills
body: Developers who maintain CI/CD workflows demonstrate DevOps skills that don't appear in `import` statements or README text. Add a parser that reads `.github/workflows/*.yml` files and extracts inferred skills (e.g., `GitHub Actions`, `Docker`, `pytest`, `deployment`).

title: Add end-to-end ingestion test with a sample resume fixture
body: The resume parser and the batch embedding processor have unit tests, but `IngestionPipeline.ingest_resume` isn't covered by any test. Add an integration test that runs a fixture from `tests/fixtures/sample_resumes/` through parsing, chunking, and embedding storage, then asserts on the returned `chunk_count`.

title: Hybrid retriever skips keyword indexing and normalizes BM25 scores per batch
body: `HybridRetriever.retrieve` fetches the collection's chunks but doesn't pass them to `keyword_searcher.index()`, so the keyword half of the blend contributes nothing. Each side is normalized by its own batch's top score, so the best keyword match would scale to 1.0 even when it's weak.

title: Vector store returns stale embeddings after a document is re-ingested
body: When a README is updated and re-ingested, the old embeddings remain in the vector store alongside the new ones. The retriever can return outdated chunks that don't reflect the current document content.

title: Review generator never combines feedback across a user's projects
body: `_consolidate_feedback` doesn't merge anything: it keeps the first section for each `section_name` and drops the rest instead of combining repeated observations. The prompts carry only context, username and project count, so per-project detail needs to reach the model too.

title: Implement a caching layer for repeated identical portfolio queries
body: When a user submits the same portfolio for review twice without making changes, the system re-runs the full RAG pipeline. Add a cache keyed on the profile's content hash that returns the stored review if the portfolio hasn't changed.

title: Implement a re-ranking step that uses an LLM to score retrieved chunks before generation
body: The current retriever uses vector + keyword scores for ranking. Add an optional re-ranking pass that prompts a smaller LLM to score each retrieved chunk's relevance to the query before passing the top-k to the generator.

title: Architecture doc doesn't explain the hybrid retrieval scoring formula
body: `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` describes that hybrid retrieval blends vector and keyword scores but doesn't explain the formula or the default weights. Add a section explaining the scoring logic with an example.

title: Add snapshot tests for prompt templates to catch accidental changes
body: Prompt templates directly affect review quality. Add snapshot tests that fail if a template's content changes without a version bump, so developers must consciously version templates rather than silently editing them.

title: Add an integration test that runs the full RAG pipeline against a mock LLM
body: `tests/integration/` holds only an empty `__init__.py`, so no test runs a query through retrieval, generation and parsing. Add one marked `@pytest.mark.integration`. `ReviewGenerator` builds its own OpenAI client, so the test needs a way to pass in a fixed response.

title: Implement an offline eval runner that measures review quality across a benchmark portfolio set
body: `scripts/run_evals.py` prints two lines and returns, and no code calls `EvalSuite`, so review quality isn't measured. `make eval` runs the script, and the RAG Evaluation workflow runs it and reads `eval_results.json`. Implement it to score the benchmark profiles and write that file.

title: Agent session state is not cleared between reviews for the same user
body: `Orchestrator` keeps one `ContextManager` and never empties it, so one orchestrator handling two reviews returns the first run's result for every tool whose input hasn't changed. Empty that cache and delete the profile's saved session state when `run` starts.

title: Failed tool calls recorded in `tool_results` never reach the review output
body: `Orchestrator.run` logs each failed tool call and records it in `tool_results` with `success: False`, but no caller reads those entries. They should reach the review output so the user sees that a tool failed.

title: Agent state isn't persisted across API restarts, causing in-progress reviews to be lost
body: Long-running reviews (5+ repositories) that span a server restart lose their progress. The in-flight session state is held only in memory and not written to Redis until completion.

title: Repo analyzer never receives a file list, so `has_tests` and `has_ci` are always `False`
body: `_detect_tests()` and `_detect_ci()` in `ingestion/parsers/repo_analyzer.py` read file names from `repo_data.get("file_structure", "")`, but no code sets that key, so `has_tests` and `has_ci` are always `False`. `GitHubTool` doesn't fetch a file list, and the analyzer needs one under `file_structure`.

title: Add a `contribution_streak` field to the GitHub analysis (longest consecutive days of commits)
body: Consistent contribution activity is a portfolio signal. Add a tool that computes the user's longest consecutive commit streak from their GitHub contribution history.

title: Implement a `DependencyAuditTool` that flags outdated major dependencies in project repos
body: Add a new tool that parses `requirements.txt`, `package.json`, or `pyproject.toml` files in submitted repos and flags dependencies that are more than one major version behind the current release.

title: Add a plan validation step that checks tool prerequisites before executing the plan
body: The orchestrator executes tools without checking their dependencies. For example, the skill extractor depends on ingestion being complete, and the market analyzer depends on the tech detector having run first. Add a DAG-based plan validator.

title: Add a mock GitHub API server for integration tests
body: `tests/integration/` holds only an `__init__.py`, and no test exercises `GitHubTool`. Add tests that point the tool's `base_url` at a local `pytest-httpserver` and cover the 404 and 403 responses, so the `test-integration` CI job can stop treating an empty suite as a pass.

title: Add an end-to-end agent test using a fully stubbed tool suite
body: There is no test that exercises the full agent lifecycle (plan → execute → synthesize) without live dependencies. Add an integration test using stub implementations of all tools and the mock LLM.

title: Injection detection misses role-switch lines with whitespace before the colon
body: The role-switch pattern in `INJECTION_PATTERNS` requires the colon right after the role word, so text like `\n System : ignore` is not detected. Allow whitespace between the role word and the colon.

title: Safety monitoring doesn't emit metrics when the content filter is bypassed by a multi-turn conversation
body: The monitoring system logs safety events for single-turn requests but doesn't track cases where a user circumvents the content filter across multiple API calls. Add cross-request pattern detection for known bypass sequences.

title: Add a safety event count to the health check endpoint
body: The `/health` endpoint in `api/routes/health.py` reports `safety_events_last_hour` as the literal `0` and never reads the safety layer, so the field doesn't reflect any recorded event. `SafetyMonitor.get_event_count()` in `safety/monitoring.py` can supply per-type counts to fill it.

title: Add a "feedback tone check" that ensures all generated feedback is written constructively
body: After generation, add a tone classification step that uses a prompt to classify whether each feedback section is constructive (actionable, specific, encouraging) or negative (discouraging, vague, dismissive). Reject and regenerate sections that fail.

title: Add rate limiting per IP address in addition to per user
body: `RateLimiter.check_rate_limit` in `safety/rate_limiter.py` accepts any identifier, but no code in `api/` calls it, so requests aren't rate limited, signed in or not. Add middleware registered in `api/main.py` that checks each request by client IP, and by user ID when a token is present.

title: Implement a red-teaming test suite for the prompt injection defense
body: Add an automated test suite that attempts a curated set of known prompt injection attacks against the safety layer and verifies that all are blocked. This suite should run in CI on every PR that touches `safety/`.

title: Add a bias audit report that runs over a sample of stored reviews
body: Implement an offline bias audit script (`scripts/audit_bias.py`) that samples 100 stored reviews, runs them through the bias detector with detailed logging, and produces a report showing false positive/negative rates by demographic signal.

title: Add integration tests for the full safety middleware chain
body: Unit tests exist for individual safety components but there's no test that runs a request through the full safety stack (prompt defense → content filter → bias detector → PII scrubber). Add an integration test with fixtures covering pass and fail cases for each layer.

title: `DELETE /profiles/{profile_id}` leaves the profile's embeddings in the vector store
body: `delete_profile` in `core/services/profile_service.py` removes the profile's database rows but leaves its chunks in the vector store, so retrieval can still return them. `ingestion/pipeline.py` stores the `profile_id` with every chunk. Clearing those chunks should be part of the deletion.

title: Concurrent review requests for the same profile can produce inconsistent results
body: If a user submits two review requests simultaneously, both requests start the agent loop against the same profile state. The second agent loop may read stale data modified by the first. Add a per-profile lock to serialize concurrent reviews.

title: Add an API rate limiting header (`X-RateLimit-Remaining`) to responses
body: `safety/rate_limiter.py` defines `check_rate_limit`, but no code in `api/` calls it, so responses don't carry an `X-RateLimit-Limit` or `X-RateLimit-Remaining` header and the API never returns `429`. Add middleware that calls it and sets both headers.

title: Implement a webhook system that notifies users when their review is ready
body: Long-running reviews (multiple repositories) can take 30–90 seconds. Add a webhook endpoint where clients can register a callback URL that receives a `POST` with the review payload when processing is complete.

title: `POST /reviews` endpoint has no test for when the profile has no ingested documents
body: There's no test that exercises the review endpoint when a profile exists but has no associated ingested content. Add a test that verifies the endpoint returns an appropriate error rather than crashing.

title: API reference doc is missing the `POST /profiles` request body schema
body: `docs/API.md` lists endpoints with a short description but doesn't give any request bodies. Add them for `POST /profiles` and `POST /reviews`, with a description and an example value for each field. `POST /profiles` takes multipart form data, not JSON.

title: Add integration tests for authentication edge cases
body: `api/middleware/auth.py` has no test coverage, and `tests/integration/` holds only an empty `__init__.py`. Add tests that call a protected endpoint with an expired token, a malformed token, no `Authorization` header, and a token signed with a different secret.

title: Review progress indicator doesn't update in real time during long-running reviews
body: The review page shows a fixed spinner, so a long review looks like the app has stopped responding. The status endpoint reports `progress_pct`, but `Review` has no such column, so it's always 0. Show a real progress bar.

title: Add a "Copy link" button to share a public review summary
body: Allow users to generate a shareable link to a read-only view of their review summary. The link should be accessible without login and expire after 30 days.

title: Add a before/after comparison view for users who have completed multiple reviews
body: The Review History table shows each review's score and date, but two reviews can't be opened together, so their sections and suggestions are never compared. Add a side-by-side view of two selected reviews.

title: Add accessibility tests for the review page using `jest-axe`
body: The review page has no automated accessibility checks. Add `jest-axe` tests that verify the page doesn't have common accessibility violations (contrast, missing labels, improper heading structure).

title: Test coverage for `core/services/review_service.py` is below 40%
body: The review service orchestrates the full review workflow and is the most critical service in the application, but most of its code paths are untested. Add unit tests targeting the major execution paths including success, partial failure, and full failure cases.

title: No property-based tests for the PII scrubber
body: The PII scrubber handles an enormous variety of personal data formats. Add property-based tests using `hypothesis` to generate randomized PII inputs and verify the scrubber always removes them.

title: Add a performance benchmark for the ingestion pipeline to detect regressions
body: Large portfolio ingestion (5 repos + resume) should complete within 30 seconds. Add a benchmark test using `pytest-benchmark` that fails if mean ingestion time exceeds the threshold.

title: API docs don't include example `curl` commands
body: `docs/API.md` describes each endpoint but has no example invocations. Developers setting up the project for the first time can't quickly verify the API is working.

title: Add `Args:`/`Returns:`/`Raises:` sections to the public function docstrings in `core/services/`
body: The docstrings on the eight public functions in `core/services/` don't have `Args:`, `Returns:` or `Raises:` sections. Add the ones that apply, matching the code: `delete_profile` re-raises after a rollback, while `process_review` sets the review to `failed` and returns.

title: Write a contributor onboarding guide that walks through a complete issue → PR lifecycle
body: `docs/SETUP.md` and `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` document the fork-to-merge path in separate sections. Write a walkthrough that follows one issue from start to finish, and add `make test-integration` to CONTRIBUTING.md's list of local checks.

title: Add a dependency vulnerability scan to the CI pipeline
body: The project has no automated check for known security vulnerabilities in its Python or JavaScript dependencies. Add a step that runs `pip audit` and `npm audit` and fails the build on high-severity findings.

title: Add a database migration validation step to CI that checks all migrations can be applied cleanly
body: Schema migrations are tested manually before merging but not in CI. Add a step that spins up a fresh database, runs all migrations in order, and verifies the schema matches the SQLAlchemy models.

title: PII scrubber fails to redact parenthesized US phone numbers
body:
The phone-number pattern in `pii_scrubber.py` matches dashed formats like `555-123-4567` but not the parenthesized format `(555) 123-4567`, so one of the most common US phone formats passes through `scrub()` unredacted, and `detect()` reports no PII for it.

**Steps to reproduce:**
```python
from safety.pii_scrubber import PIIScrubber
s = PIIScrubber()
print(s.scrub('Call me at (555) 123-4567 or 555-123-4567'))
# observed: 'Call me at (555) 123-4567 or [REDACTED]'
print(s.detect('Call me at (555) 123-4567'))
# observed: []
```
Related failing tests: `test_us_phone_number_redaction`, `test_us_phone_formats`, `test_detect_phone_pii`, `test_phone_at_start_of_text` in `tests/unit/test_pii_scrubber.py`.

title: Resume section detection fails on text with leading whitespace
body:
`_detect_sections()` in `resume_parser.py` anchors every section-header pattern at the start of a line (`^Experience`, `\nExperience`). Text extracted from PDFs commonly preserves leading indentation, and for such input no sections are detected at all — `detected_sections` comes back empty.

**Steps to reproduce:**
```python
from ingestion.parsers.resume_parser import ResumeParser
r = ResumeParser()
res = r.parse('\n    John Smith\n    john@example.com\n\n    Education:\n    - B.S. Computer Science\n\n    Skills: Python\n')
print(res.metadata['detected_sections'])
# observed: []  (expected: Education, Skills)
```
Related failing tests: `test_parse_single_column_resume_text`, `test_parse_resume_no_work_experience`, `test_detect_sections` in `tests/unit/test_resume_parser.py`.

title: Skill extractor fails to detect JavaScript and TypeScript
body:
The JavaScript and TypeScript checks in `_detect_languages` (`ingestion/parsers/skill_extractor.py`) read `.js` and `.ts` from the `filename` argument only, plus an `import`/`require` pattern and `package.json` from the text. JavaScript or TypeScript described any other way doesn't get a language entry. `_detect_tools` and `_detect_databases` match a technology only when its own name appears in the text.

**Steps to reproduce:** `pytest tests/unit/test_skill_extractor.py -q` — `test_javascript_detection`, `test_text_with_typescript_files`, `test_devops_tool_detection`, `test_docker_compose_detection` and `test_database_technology_detection` fail their assertions and report as `xfailed`.

title: Structural chunker silently drops documents that contain no headings
body:
`StructuralChunker.chunk()` returns an empty list for any document without markdown headings, so the entire document is silently excluded from the RAG index instead of being chunked as a single block or falling back to another strategy.

**Steps to reproduce:**
```python
from ingestion.chunking.structural_chunker import StructuralChunker
c = StructuralChunker()
print(len(c.chunk('This is a plain document with no headings at all. ' * 20, {})))
# observed: 0  (a ~1000-char document produces no chunks)
```
Related failing test: `test_document_with_no_headings` in `tests/unit/test_structural_chunker.py`.

title: Tech detector counts vendored and build-output files, skewing language detection
body:
`tech_detector.py` does not exclude `node_modules/` or `build/` paths. A repo with 2 Python source files and 6 vendored/bundled JS files is reported as primarily JavaScript.

**Steps to reproduce:**
```python
from agent.tools.tech_detector import TechDetector
t = TechDetector()
files = ['main.py','core/app.py','node_modules/lib/index.js','node_modules/lib/util.js','node_modules/x/a.js','node_modules/y/b.js','build/bundle.js','build/vendor.js']
print(t.execute({'files': files}).data['primary_language'])
# observed: 'JavaScript'  (expected: 'Python')
```
Related failing tests: `test_node_modules_excluded`, `test_build_directory_excluded` in `tests/unit/test_tech_detector.py`.

title: Bias detector patterns are too narrow to match common phrasings
body:
The regex patterns in `bias_detector.py` require near-exact phrase sequences (e.g. “bootcamp graduates lack rigor”) and miss natural phrasings of the same bias, such as “The candidate only attended a bootcamp, so this project lacks the rigor of a formal CS education” or age-based assumptions like “Given their age, they likely cannot keep up with modern frameworks”. Nine unit tests specifying the intended coverage fail.

**Steps to reproduce:**
```python
from safety.bias_detector import BiasDetector
print(BiasDetector.detect_bias('The candidate only attended a bootcamp, so this project lacks the rigor of a formal CS education'))
# observed: (False, '')  (expected: flagged as dismissive educational-background language)
```
Related failing tests: 9 tests in `tests/unit/test_bias_detector.py` (e.g. `test_dismissive_bootcamp_language_detected`, `test_demographic_assumption_age_detected`).

title: Faithfulness checker scores claims unsupported when the context uses different words
body:
`_is_supported()` in `faithfulness_checker.py` marks a claim supported only when it shares two or more words with the context, stop words excluded, so “Knows Python” scores 0.0 against “python expert” but 1.0 against “The candidate knows Python”. Support should not depend on shared wording.

**Steps to reproduce:** `pytest tests/unit/test_faithfulness_checker.py -q` — observed: `assert 0.0 > 0.5` fails in `test_multiple_context_chunks`.

title: Faithfulness checker crashes when a context chunk has `text: None`
body:
`check()` builds the context with `chunk.get("text", "")`, but when the key is present with value `None`, `.get()` returns `None` (the default applies only to missing keys), and the subsequent `" ".join(...)` raises `TypeError`.

**Steps to reproduce:**
```python
from rag.evaluator.faithfulness_checker import FaithfulnessChecker
FaithfulnessChecker().check('Knows Python.', [{'text': None}])
# observed: TypeError: sequence item 0: expected str instance, NoneType found
```
Related failing test: `test_none_context_chunk_text` in `tests/unit/test_faithfulness_checker.py`.

title: Health check DB probe passes a raw SQL string, which fails under SQLAlchemy 2.x
body:
The database probe in `api/routes/health.py` executes the literal string "SELECT 1". SQLAlchemy 2.x requires textual SQL to be wrapped in `sqlalchemy.text()`, so the probe raises and the health check reports the database as down even when it is reachable.

**Steps to reproduce:** call `GET /health` with the stack running (or invoke the route handler in a unit test with a live session) and observe the database check failing with `ArgumentError: Textual SQL expression 'SELECT 1' should be explicitly declared as text('SELECT 1')`.

title: Health check references `settings.redis_host`, which does not exist on Settings
body:
The Redis probe in `api/routes/health.py` builds its client from `settings.redis_host` and `settings.redis_port`. `Settings` in `core/config.py` doesn't define either field; it carries a single `redis_url`, which the probe should use instead. The probe's `except Exception` catches the resulting `AttributeError`, so the health check reports Redis as down even when it is reachable.

**Steps to reproduce:** call `GET /health` with Redis running and observe a 503 whose body reports `"redis": "unhealthy"`, with `redis_health_check_failed` and an `AttributeError` for `redis_host` in the log.

title: README scorer test fixture is too short for its own word-count assertion
body:
`test_readme_with_all_quality_signals` asserts `data["word_count"] > 100` and `word_count_category == "comprehensive"`, but its fixture README contains only ~51 words, so the test fails against correct scorer behavior. Extend the fixture (or correct the assertion) so the test validates what it intends to.

**Steps to reproduce:** `pytest tests/unit/test_readme_scorer.py -q` — observed: `assert 51 > 100` fails.

title: Relevance scorer “partial overlap” test fixture actually has full query overlap
body:
`test_query_with_partial_overlap` uses query “Python Django web framework” against a chunk containing all four query terms, then asserts the score is below 0.9. The scorer correctly returns 1.0 for full keyword coverage, so the test fails against correct behavior. Fix the fixture so the overlap is genuinely partial.

**Steps to reproduce:** `pytest tests/unit/test_relevance_scorer.py -q` — observed: `assert 1.0 < 0.9` fails.

title: review_service unit tests misconfigure async mocks — 13 of 19 tests fail
body:
The service code correctly awaits `db.execute(...)`, but the tests build their mock session so that `result.scalars()` returns a coroutine, causing `AttributeError: 'coroutine' object has no attribute 'first'` (and `'all'`) inside otherwise-correct service code. Rework the mock setup (e.g. `AsyncMock` for `execute`, `MagicMock` for the result object) so the existing CRUD tests actually run.

**Steps to reproduce:** `pytest tests/unit/test_review_service.py -q` — observed: 13 failed, 6 passed.

title: structlog output is not captured by pytest caplog — log assertions fail suite-wide
body:
The application logs through structlog, which is not configured to propagate into the stdlib logging system during tests. Every test asserting on `caplog` (e.g. `test_empty_chunks_list_returns_empty` in `tests/unit/test_batch_processor.py`) fails even though the code under test does emit the expected log event. Configure structlog in `tests/conftest.py` (e.g. via `structlog.stdlib` processors or `capture_logs`) so caplog-based assertions work.

**Steps to reproduce:** `pytest tests/unit/test_batch_processor.py::TestBatchEmbeddingProcessor::test_empty_chunks_list_returns_empty -q` — observed: assertion on caplog fails while the warning is visibly printed to stderr.

title: Review creation does not verify profile ownership
body:
## Problem

The `POST /reviews` endpoint passes the authenticated user's ID to `create_review()`, but `core/services/review_service.py` ignores that argument when creating a review.

The service creates a `Review` from the supplied `profile_id` without checking that the profile belongs to the current user. This is inconsistent with `get_review()` and `list_reviews()`, which already scope review reads through `Profile.user_id`.

## Impact

An authenticated user who knows another user's profile UUID may be able to create a review for that profile by sending:

```text
POST /reviews
{"profile_id": "<another-users-profile-id>"}

title: Keyword search raises `ZeroDivisionError` when the index is empty
body:
`KeywordSearcher.index()` passes its tokenized corpus to `BM25Okapi`, so `index([])` raises `ZeroDivisionError` inside the rank-bm25 library. `search()` handles the empty case and returns an empty list, and `index()` shouldn't raise on an empty corpus either.

The covering test is marked `@pytest.mark.xfail` referencing manifest id H-01 — remove the marker as part of the fix.

title: Output parser crashes on a top-level JSON array fallback
body:
When the LLM returns a top-level JSON array instead of an object, `output_parser.py` calls `.items()` on the parsed value and raises `AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'items'`. The fallback path should handle array responses.

The covering test is marked `@pytest.mark.xfail` referencing manifest id H-02 — remove the marker as part of the fix.

title: README parser test fixture is indented, so it contains no headings
body:
`test_parse_standard_readme` asserts `heading_count > 0` for the `sample_readme_text` fixture, but every line of text in it is indented four spaces, so the parser finds no headings. The parser isn't wrong; the fixture shouldn't be indented.

The covering test is marked `@pytest.mark.xfail` referencing manifest id H-03 — remove the marker as part of the fix.

title: Heading hierarchy test fixture is indented, so it contains no headings
body:
`test_extract_heading_hierarchy` builds its markdown from lines indented by eight spaces, which Markdown treats as a code block. `_extract_heading_hierarchy` doesn't find any headings there, so the test fails against correct parser behavior. Remove the indentation.

The covering test is marked `@pytest.mark.xfail` referencing manifest id H-04 — remove the marker as part of the fix.

title: `verify_password` raises `UnknownHashError` on malformed stored hashes instead of returning False
body:
`core/security.py` lets passlib's `UnknownHashError` escape when the stored hash is not a recognizable format. Verification against a malformed hash should fail closed (return `False`), not raise.

The covering test is marked `@pytest.mark.xfail` referencing manifest id H-05 — remove the marker as part of the fix.

title: README and `.env.example` disagree about which LLM API key to set
body: `README.md` tells you to add `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` to `.env`, but `.env.example` doesn't list that variable, and its comment offers only `mock` and `openai` for `LLM_PROVIDER`. `core/config.py` defines both keys. Make the two files agree.
